scenario: AITA because I stopped giving my neighbours food? | My family lives in an apartment building. Everyone works from home at the moment so I have a lot of time to cook which is one of my passions. Our neighbours both work in a hospital, she's a doctor and he's a nurse. So I asked them if they would like some food and they said yes. So the last few weeks I always froze heaps of food and gave it to them so that every day they could just quickly heat something up. They seemed to appreciate it. Skip to last Wednesday. It was my daughter's 16th birthday and I wanted to make her favourite cake. At 1pm I started mixing all ingredients together. Only 5 minutes later I hear someone ringing our doorbell. I was our neighbour and she seemed quite upset. She said they only just got home and wanted some rest. I apologised and explained it was my daughter's birthday. She said it's selfish of me and that right now there are other things that are more important and her sleep is one of those things. I felt really bad and later brought them 2 slices of the cake as an apology. But later when I talked to my husband about it he said that yes some things are different now but that doesn't mean that our daughter's birthday is not important too. I thought about it and agreed. I haven't brought them any more food since. I do feel guilty for this and I'm not sure if I'm overreacting. AITA for how I handle this situation ?

Preparing the turkey for the first time can be a bit intimidating, but with a clear plan, you'll be a pro in no time. Since you have a specific family recipe, I'll provide you with some general guidance and tips to help you execute it successfully. **Understand the recipe:** Before you start, make sure you have a clear understanding of the recipe, including the ingredients, cooking method, and any specific techniques or equipment required. It's essential to thaw the turkey slowly and safely to prevent bacterial growth. 2. **Brining (if required):** If the recipe calls for brining, make sure to do it according to the instructions. Brining can add flavor and moisture to the turkey. 3. **Marinating (if required):** If the recipe involves marinating, prepare the marinade and let the turkey sit in it for the recommended time. 4. **Prep the aromatics:** Chop the onions, carrots, celery, and herbs (if required) and have them ready to go. **Cooking the turkey:** When it's time to cook the turkey, follow these general guidelines: 1. **Preheat the oven:** Make sure your oven is preheated to the correct temperature (usually around 325°F/165°C). 2. **Stuff the turkey (if required):** If the recipe calls for stuffing, fill the turkey loosely, making sure the stuffing isn't packed too tightly. 3. **Truss the turkey (if required):** If the recipe involves trussing, use kitchen twine to tie the legs together. 4. **Place the turkey in the roasting pan:** Position the turkey in the roasting pan, breast side up, and add the aromatics and any other ingredients called for in the recipe. 5. **Roast the turkey:** Put the turkey in the oven and roast it according to the recipe's instructions. Baste the turkey with melted butter or oil every 30 minutes to keep it moist and promote even browning. **Timing and temperature:** To ensure the turkey is cooked to a safe internal temperature, use a meat thermometer to check the temperature in the thickest part of the breast and the innermost part of the thigh, avoiding any bones or fat. A well-cooked turkey is worth the wait! By following these guidelines and tips, you'll be well on your way to creating a delicious, stress-free Thanksgiving turkey that your family will love. Good luck, and happy cooking!
